title: Trump's 2024 Grocery Photo Op Now Haunts Republicans Ahead of Midterms
excerpt: Polls show 65% of Americans find groceries unaffordable and voters give Democrats a slight edge on the economy for the first time in nearly a decade, as rising food prices turn into the top issue for November's elections.
body:
• A Reuters analysis found grocery prices have risen 3.4% in the first 19 months of Trump's second term, with beef up 19.2%, coffee up nearly 23%, and apples up 14%.
  • Trump's net approval rating on cost of living has plummeted to -47%, his weakest issue by a wide margin, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.
  • A Washington Post/Ipsos poll found 65% of Americans say groceries are unaffordable and 54% of registered voters cite the economy as the top factor in their midterm vote.
  • Voters now give Democrats a slight edge over Republicans on economic stewardship for the first time in nearly a decade.

Two years after Donald Trump stood between tables of fruit, beef, and cereal at his Bedminster golf club to blame Democrats for high food prices, those same grocery staples have become a symbol of the gap between his promises and the reality facing American shoppers — and a growing vulnerability for Republicans heading into November's midterm elections.

The Numbers Don't Lie

A Reuters analysis of 26 grocery categories tracked by the Bureau of Labor Statistics found prices have risen 3.4% in the first 19 months of Trump's second term. That is less than a quarter of the pace at the same point under Biden, but falls far short of Trump's pledge to actually lower prices.

https://x.com/YourAnonNews/status/2089366649237577864

The increases are concentrated in items that hit household budgets hard. Uncooked beef has jumped 19.2%. Coffee is up nearly 23%. Fresh fish and seafood rose 8.6%. Apples climbed 14%. Eggs are among just six of the 26 categories showing declines — down nearly 40%, reflecting a market correction after avian flu-driven shortages, not administration policy.

A White House official pointed to July CPI data showing minimal month-over-month increases, calling it "further proof that President Trump's long-term agenda is delivering." But voters are not buying the optimism.

Voters Turn Sour

A Reuters/Ipsos poll concluded earlier this month found Trump's net approval rating on his handling of the cost of living at -47%, down from -6% at the start of his term. It is his weakest issue by a wide margin, trailing his ratings on the economy (-35%) and immigration (-16%).

A separate Washington Post/Ipsos poll conducted July 8–13 found that 65% of Americans consider groceries unaffordable, 48% expect the economy to worsen over the next year, and 59% of Americans with incomes under $50,000 say they cannot improve their standard of living.

"I expect the same anti-incumbent shift to happen in 2026, this time possibly weakening Republicans. Each time one does it, it is the equivalent of a campaign ad against the incumbent."

— Francesco Trebbi, Public Policy Professor, UC Berkeley

For the first time in nearly a decade, voters give Democrats a slight edge over Republicans on who they trust to handle the economy — though neither party commands a strong advantage, with 34% trusting Republicans, 33% Democrats, and 26% trusting neither.

Republican Enthusiasm Wanes

Reuters interviewed 17 Republicans and independents in New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, a battleground that includes Bedminster. More than half said they were either undecided or leaning toward the Democratic challenger, Rebecca Bennett, over Republican incumbent Tom Kean.

Sheila Carney, a 68-year-old Trump voter near Bedminster, described unloading $70 worth of groceries — some meat, detergent, and a 12-pack of iced tea — as evidence that Trump's promises have not materialized.

"This is real. He can say it's not, but it is. He hasn't brought anything down."

— Sheila Carney, Trump voter, New Jersey

Carney, a hospital administration assistant who has delayed retirement while helping pay off her son's student loans, said high grocery and gasoline prices — the latter driven partly by the Iran war — were among the reasons she might sit out the midterms entirely.

The Indian-American Factor

Indian Americans, one of the wealthiest and most politically active immigrant communities in the United States, are concentrated in suburban swing districts like New Jersey's 7th. As significant campaign donors and an increasingly decisive voting bloc, their response to economic conditions could amplify the broader trend. Rising costs affect everyone, but for dual-income South Asian households often supporting extended families across continents, the squeeze on purchasing power resonates on multiple fronts.

What's at Stake

The economy and cost of living ranked as the top two issues for registered voters across all parties in midterm polling — rated 7.7 to 8.5 out of 10 in importance regardless of party affiliation. Bennett, a military veteran, has campaigned on undoing Trump's tariffs and restoring food stamp benefits. "Beef is very expensive, so we don't buy beef anymore," she told Reuters.

Whether the grocery aisle translates into the ballot box remains to be seen. But for Republicans, the image of Trump surrounded by groceries he promised to make cheaper is proving difficult to shake.
nri_angle: Indian Americans concentrated in suburban swing districts are among the most politically active immigrant communities, and rising costs affect households often supporting extended families across continents.
author: Diaspora Desk
